note: Track harmony-line, step 1: hold Sol, then Mi, against the drone's Do, then hold Sol while the backing track moves between {{chord:I}} and {{chord:V}}, counted the long way. The key and the slow tempo (40 up to 60) are moves, so the old Key selector is gone and the other-key line is marked {{?key}}. missing: a tool that sounds a second note or a moving line against the singer's held note (the staff's drone can only sound Do).

exercise.title: Hold your note against another one
exercise.why: Singing harmony starts with keeping your own note while a different one sounds, so you hold Sol or Mi against the drone's Do and listen to the two notes together.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff. The drone holds Do. Tap the low {{5}}, the ringed note, to hear it, then hold it for one easy breath. Sing it on "oo".
Practice until your line stays level while the drone sounds.
_Don't reach for high notes: take the low {{5}}, the one nearest the drone._

Press Start exercise below to start the drone and the mic. Now your note is the low {{3}}, the ringed note, which sits closer to the drone's Do. Tap it to hear it, then hold it. Sing it on "oo".
If your line slides down towards Do, tap {{3}} again and start the note fresh.
{{?key}}In another key both notes are new, and yours is still Sol or Mi against the drone's Do.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together, at {{=bpm}}. The backing track plays {{chord:I}} and {{chord:V}} in turn, one bar each.
{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, and {{chord:V}} is the 5th chord, built on {{5}}. {{5}} is in both, so sing the low {{5}} and hold it through each change. Sing it on "oo".
Practice until your line stays level when the chord box changes.
